title: PT-Map: Efficient Program Transformation Optimization for CGRA Mapping
problem: Existing CGRA mapping approaches lack systematic exploration of the transformation space and efficient evaluation of transformation candidates, resulting in suboptimal performance and energy efficiency outcomes. Traditional methods cannot comprehensively explore transformation combinations or quickly predict their performance impact.
motivation: Program transformation is critical for optimizing performance and energy efficiency in CGRA mapping, as it complements loop scheduling in exploiting the spatial-temporal reconfigurability of these parallel architectures.
method: PT-Map maps out all possible ways to optimize and transform a program for a CGRA (a reconfigurable processor that can be rewired for different computations). It explores these transformations systematically using a top-down strategy—starting with broad approaches and narrowing to specific candidates. Rather than testing each candidate by simulating the actual hardware, PT-Map uses a graph neural network (a machine learning model that learns how interconnected components behave) to quickly predict which transformations will perform well, guided by the CGRA's architectural parameters.
key_novelty: PT-Map combines graph neural network prediction with top-down transformation exploration to enable efficient CGRA mapping without full hardware simulation.
contributions: Comprehensive transformation space definition for CGRA mapping
Bottom-up evaluation scheme using architectural parameters
GNN-based predictive model for rapid transformation evaluation

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 59.0% EDP reduction vs MapZero, 23.2% vs PBP

primary_theme: efficient program transformation optimization for reconfigurable arrays
